clue.text: Interview a young attendant and discharge

parts.note: to interview someone is to see them, as in 'the manager will see you now'
a page is a boy who attends a knight, a bride or a hotel guest

explanation.surface: An instruction about questioning a junior servant and then dismissing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads as a verb, sacking the young attendant, but it is a noun: a slow leak of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow escape of liquid through a crack or porous material is a leak or discharge.

clue.text: The American cowboy's topping!

parts.note: 'topping' is slang for what goes on top of the head, so the clue asks for a cowboy's broad-brimmed hat, not a pizza garnish

explanation.definitionFit: The wide-brimmed felt hat is the classic headgear of the American West, named after its Philadelphia maker.

clue.text: The leader or aide lit out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the chief or an assistant has illuminated something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges OR AIDE LIT. 'Leader' is not a person: it is the newspaper sense, the main opinion article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers the leader, or leading article, is the column giving the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: A portion set aside

parts.note: a portion is a part or share of something

explanation.surface: A share of something reserved for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed separately from the rest, kept away from the group, is set aside.

clue.text: Gas is in general more desirable than ever

indicators.note: the gas is said to be in the words that follow, so its letters run inside them, across the end of 'desirable', all of 'than' and the start of 'ever'

explanation.surface: A claim that gas is now generally better value than it has ever been.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans three words: the last letter of 'desirable', 'than', and the first letter of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless hydrocarbon found in natural gas, with two carbon atoms, is a gas at room temperature.

clue.text: Having rested, one dined, so content

parts.note: having rested on a chair, one sat
the Roman numeral for one is I
dined means ate

explanation.surface: Someone sits down, eats a meal and feels contented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like an adjective describing the diner, but it is a verb: to fill or satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to satisfy their appetite fully, to fill them up.

clue.text: Press men at one time in China

definitions.meaning: to press men was to force them into service as sailors, as press gangs did in past centuries
a great port city on China's east coast

explanation.surface: A remark that journalists were once stationed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press men' suggests journalists; it means pressing men into service. The verb comes from sailors drugged and carried aboard ships bound for the Chinese port.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone for service at sea is to press them; the Chinese seaport gave its name to the practice, and is itself a place in China.

clue.text: Coming to and bearing with everything involved

indicators.note: involved means taken inside, so the word for everything goes within the word for carrying

parts.note: bearing, in the sense of carrying, is toting
everything means all

explanation.surface: Someone arriving while carrying a load with all their belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to' sounds like regaining consciousness; it is the sum sense, as in 'the bill comes to ten pounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is coming to a certain sum is adding up, or amounting, to it.

clue.text: Generous politician getting in beer

indicators.note: the politician is getting into the beer, so those letters go inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
MP stands for Member of Parliament, a British politician

explanation.surface: An open-handed politician buying a round of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous helping is a plentiful or abundant one.

clue.text: Tried a new variety of seed, say

indicators.note: a new variety is a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the following two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A gardener who has tested a new strain of seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A new variety of' rearranges SEED and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: To have essayed something is to have attempted it, an old formal sense.

clue.text: Grave expression of appreciation

parts.note: 'grave' suggests serious, but it is the burial place: words of praise carved on a tomb

explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a headstone usually praises the dead person, a tribute literally at the graveside.

clue.text: He granted Salome's request — but not for dancing!

parts.note: to be not for something is to be against it, anti
a pas is a step in dancing, especially in ballet

explanation.surface: An ironic aside that the ruler who rewarded Salome's dance disapproved of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Salome danced for Herod and asked for the head of John the Baptist; the Herod who agreed is known by this second name. The surface's 'but' is irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod the tetrarch of Galilee, who had John the Baptist beheaded after Salome danced for him, bore this name.

clue.text: Where people aim to make a hit

definitions.text: Where people aim to make a hit

parts.words: Where people aim to make a hit
parts.note: 'aim to make a hit' sounds like ambition for a success, but read literally it is people pointing guns at targets

explanation.definitionFit: A fairground booth or indoor range where customers fire at targets is a place for aiming and hitting.

clue.text: Nymphs in a sad muddle

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters of 'in a sad' are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mythical maidens in an unhappy state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muddle' rearranges all of IN A SAD, including 'in', which looks like a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the water nymphs who live in springs, rivers and lakes are a class of nymph.

clue.text: Loss due to smart egg-head being in a hole

indicators.note: these pieces are being put into the hole, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or hole pressed into a surface
smart, meaning neat and tidy, is trim
the head of 'egg' is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clever intellectual suffers a setback by being stuck in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg-head' looks like an intellectual, but it gives only the first letter of 'egg'; 'being in' sets the smart pieces inside the hole after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or damage suffered, a loss.

clue.text: Many got into line when stigmatised

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so it can stand for many
to get into line is to be aligned

explanation.surface: A crowd forming a queue while being publicly shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: M for 'many' is a crossword convention, from the Roman numeral for 1,000.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stigmatised is to be spoken of with contempt, slandered or vilified.

clue.text: Odd lot — can run at night

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters that follow are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A strange crowd that can only operate after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges LOT, CAN and RUN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something active or happening by night, like an owl or a bat, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Situation vacant. Write without obligation

parts.note: a situation is a job, or a post
a vacant seat is free

explanation.surface: A job advertisement inviting applicants to write in with no commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a newspaper's job column, 'Situations vacant'. Old adverts invited readers to write in without obligation, the postage already paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply sent with the postage paid by the advertiser costs nothing, so readers may write without any obligation.

clue.text: Telling Auntie?

definitions.meaning: telling a story means narrating it, a narration
an aunt is a member of the family, a relative; the question mark admits she is just one example

explanation.definitionFit: A telling is a narration or account of events, and an aunt is a family member or kinsperson.

clue.text: Withdraw troops over a wide area

indicators.note: in a down clue the troops are placed over, on top of, the wide area

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army troops
a tract is a large stretch of land

explanation.surface: An army pulling its soldiers back across an expanse of country.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or pull in, as a cat's claws or a statement.

clue.text: In which soldiers may well take a dip

definitions.text: In which soldiers may well take a dip

parts.words: In which soldiers may well take a dip
parts.note: in Britain 'soldiers' are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, not troops going for a swim

explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for a boiled egg is where toast fingers are dunked into the yolk at breakfast.

clue.text: Articles produced by men of clay

definitions.text: Articles produced by men of clay

parts.words: Articles produced by men of clay
parts.note: 'men of clay' suggests weak mortals, but read literally they are craftsmen who shape clay on a wheel

explanation.definitionFit: Pots, vases and dishes made by potters from fired clay are ceramic ware.

clue.text: Risk getting tough about a final letter

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for tough goes around the other letters

parts.note: something tough is hard
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Taking a firm stand on the last letter is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD is split after its first letter to take A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a danger or chance of harm, a risk.

clue.text: Consider how to get a tin tack out once bent

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the five words are rearranged

explanation.surface: How to pull out a crooked tin tack, once it has been bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' rearranges all fifteen letters of A TIN TACK OUT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something in mind when deciding, to allow for it, is to consider it.

clue.text: A swindler at cards?

parts.note: the clue looks like a card sharp, but it names a dishonest rogue who is also a court card, the jack

explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest rogue, and also the old name for the jack in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Body of police surrounding the monarch

indicators.note: the police are surrounding the monarch, so their letters go around the royal letter

parts.note: cops are police officers
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A force of police officers protecting the king.
explanation.walkthrough: R for a monarch comes from Latin Rex (king) or Regina (queen), as in royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is an organised body of people, such as the diplomatic corps or an army unit.

clue.text: A finish to the game the old city finds unprofessional

parts.note: checkmate, or mate, ends a game of chess
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone who wins in an ancient city is judged less than expert.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Sumerian city, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for love, not payment, and so is not a professional.

clue.text: Fix for Argentinian leaders to travel over

parts.note: the leading letters, the first two, of 'Argentinian'
to range over country is to travel across it

explanation.surface: A plan for Argentina's rulers to make a trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is plural, so it takes the first two letters of 'Argentinian', not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a meeting is to arrange or organise it.

clue.text: Ill-written letters offering support

indicators.note: badly written, so the letters of the word 'letters' are set down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Badly written letters that nevertheless offer backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-written' rearranges the word LETTERS itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of a beam on splayed legs, used to support a tabletop.

clue.text: Reveal underworld drama

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A theatre production set in the underworld is unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis, the Roman underworld, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to show it openly, to reveal it.
